'''Gillian Anne Gehring''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE|HonFInstP}} (born '''Gillian Anne Murray''', 19 May 1941) is a British academic physicist, and emeritus Professor of Physics in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/physics/people/emeritus-and-honorary|title=Emeritus, honorary and visiting staff &#124; Physics and Astronomy &#124; The University of Sheffield|date=1 December 2020|website=www.sheffield.ac.uk}}</ref> She was the second woman in the UK to become a Professor of Physics and in 2009 won the [[Nevill Mott Medal and Prize]].

==Early life and education==
Gehring was born in [[Nottingham]].<ref name=":0">[https://www2.le.ac.uk/institution/athena-swan/old-pages/inspiring-women/setbook.pdf Women in science and engineering]</ref> She lived at 42 Roland Avenue in [[Nuthall]], and attended [[Nottingham Girls' High School]]. She was at school with Rosalind Pope, who also studied Physics at Manchester.<ref>''Nottingham Evening Post'' Thursday 27 September 1990, page 8</ref> 

She studied Physics at the [[Victoria University of Manchester]] from 1959 to 1962 and from 1962 to 1963 she studied for the Diploma in Advanced Studies. She was the third woman to get a first since the war.<ref>''Nottingham Evening Post'' Saturday 15 September 1962, page 7</ref> From 1963 to 1965, she studied for a DPhil in [[Department of Physics, University of Oxford|Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of Oxford]].

==Career and research==
From 1965 to 1968, Gehring was a [[Leverhulme Fellow]] at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]], and then a NATO fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]].<ref name=":0" /> From 1968 to 1989, Gehring was a lecturer in the Department of Theoretical Physics and a Tutorial Fellow at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=support |first=Versantus |date=2026-03-23 |title=Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics {{!}} University of Oxford Department of Physics |url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/research/subdepartment/rudolf-peierls-centre-theoretical-physics |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=www.physics.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> From 1989 to 2006, Gehring was Professor of [[Solid-state physics|Solid-State Physics]] at the [[University of Sheffield]] and was the only female professor in the Physics department.

Beyond her scientific research, Gehring has played an influential role in scientific administration and editorial work. She served on editorial and advisory boards of journals including the ''[[Journal of Physics: Condensed Matter]]'', ''[[Europhysics Letters]]'', and was a founding member of the ''[[New Journal of Physics]]'' editorial board.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Honorary Fellows: Professor Gillian Gehring, OBE {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/honorary-fellowship/our-honorary-fellows/professor-gillian-gehring |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref>

Gehring has an interest in [[women in science]]. She sat on the Administrative Board of the European Platform for Women in Science, served on the [[Institute of Physics]]’ Women in Physics Group, and chaired the Women’s Group of the [[European Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2003-07-01|title=Equity for women in physics|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/equity-for-women-in-physics/|access-date=2021-03-14|website=Physics World|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Sheffield|first=University of|date=2015-03-03|title=Inspirational female physicist honoured at University - Archive - News archive - The University of Sheffield|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/news/nr/female-physicist-portrait-woman-sheffield-university-1.445697.html|access-date=2021-03-14|website=www.sheffield.ac.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref>

She also participated in government working parties such as the one that produced ''Rising Tide'' on women in science, and leading delegations at international conferences on women in physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Gillian A. Gehring • European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |url=https://epws.org/individual-member/prof-gillian-a-gehring/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Gehring's research field is theoretical and experimental magnetism, and she has made major contributions to research projects concerned with [[orbital ordering]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zenia |first=H |last2=Gehring |first2=G A |last3=Temmerman |first3=W M |date=2005-12-29 |title=Orbital ordering in cubic LaMnO 3 from first principles calculations |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/7/1/257 |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=7 |pages=257–257 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/7/1/257 |issn=1367-2630|arxiv=cond-mat/0510311 }}</ref> and the co-operative [[Jahn–Teller effect|Jahn-Teller effect]], a mechanism of [[spontaneous symmetry breaking]] that influences structural and magnetic properties of solids.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gehring |first=G A |last2=Gehring |first2=K A |date=1975-01-01 |title=Co-operative Jahn-Teller effects |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0034-4885/38/1/001 |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |volume=38 |issue=1 |pages=1–89 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/38/1/001 |issn=0034-4885|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

She was among the first to provide microscopic theories of linear birefringence in crystals undergoing [[Jahn–Teller effect|Jahn–Teller]] and magnetic transitions and to apply density matrix renormalisation group methods to study quantum phase transitions, including [[Generalization|generalisations]] that account for finite temperatures.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Becker |first=P.J. |last2=Gehring |first2=G.A. |date=1975 |title=Linear birefringence in magnetic and cooperative Jahn-Teller rare earth salts |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0038109875900782 |journal=Solid State Communications |language=en |volume=16 |issue=6 |pages=795–798 |doi=10.1016/0038-1098(75)90078-2|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

At the [[University of Sheffield]], Gehring expanded her research into magnetic oxides and related materials, establishing a research group that became internationally recognised for studies of magnetic properties in mixed‑valent compounds such as ''[[Iron(II,III) oxide|Fe₃O₄]]'' (magnetite) and perovskite manganites.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=EPWS |date=2009-07-09 |title=2009 Mott medal and prize - Prof. Gillian Gehring • European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |url=https://epws.org/2009-mott-medal-and-prize-prof-gillian-gehring/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=European Platform of Women Scientists EPWS |language=en-US}}</ref> 

She also helped initiate work on magnetically doped [[zinc oxide]] (ZnO) — including some of the first clear evidence of room‑temperature ferromagnetism in Mn‑doped ZnO — a topic of interest for potential spintronic applications.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gehring |first=Gillian A. |last2=Ahmed |first2=Mahrous R. |last3=Crombie |first3=Alex J. |date=2009-04-01 |title=Theory of magnetism with temporal disorder applied to magnetically doped ZnO |url=https://pubs.aip.org/jap/article/105/7/07E325/369458/Theory-of-magnetism-with-temporal-disorder-applied |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |language=en |volume=105 |issue=7 |doi=10.1063/1.3078007 |issn=0021-8979|arxiv=0901.4947 }}</ref> 

Her work spans theoretical models and experimental collaborations that explore how oxygen vacancies, cation substitution, and exchange interactions affect magnetic behaviour in thin films and [[Oxide|oxides]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Saeedi |first=Ahmad M. A. |last2=Gerriu |first2=Fatma M. |last3=Ying |first3=Minju |last4=Alshammari |first4=Marzook S. |last5=Heald |first5=Steve M. |last6=Li |first6=Xiaoli |last7=Blythe |first7=Harry J. |last8=Fox |first8=A. Mark |last9=Gehring |first9=Gillian A. |date=2019 |title=Competing magnetic effects due to the incorporation of oxygen in thin films of (ZnCo)O |url=https://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=C9RA06899F |journal=RSC Advances |language=en |volume=9 |issue=65 |pages=38001–38010 |doi=10.1039/C9RA06899F |issn=2046-2069 |pmc=9075728 |pmid=35541797}}</ref>

Gehring has published over 230 scientific papers, with total citations exceeding 7,000 and an h‑index of about 35, reflecting the broad influence of her work in condensed matter physics.<ref name=":2" /> 

Her most highly cited papers include studies on [[ferromagnetism]] in doped [[Zinc oxide|ZnO]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sharma |first=Parmanand |last2=Gupta |first2=Amita |last3=Rao |first3=K. V. |last4=Owens |first4=Frank J. |last5=Sharma |first5=Renu |last6=Ahuja |first6=Rajeev |last7=Guillen |first7=J. M. Osorio |last8=Johansson |first8=Börje |last9=Gehring |first9=G. A. |date=2003 |title=Ferromagnetism above room temperature in bulk and transparent thin films of Mn-doped ZnO |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat984 |journal=Nature Materials |language=en |volume=2 |issue=10 |pages=673–677 |doi=10.1038/nmat984 |issn=1476-4660|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and cooperative [[Jahn–Teller effect|Jahn–Teller effects]], which have shaped ongoing research into magnetic semiconductors and lattice–electron coupling phenomena.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gehring |first=G A |last2=Gehring |first2=K A |date=1975-01-01 |title=Co-operative Jahn-Teller effects |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0034-4885/38/1/001 |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |volume=38 |issue=1 |pages=1–89 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/38/1/001 |issn=0034-4885|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In addition to traditional [[Magnetism|magnetism topics]], Gehring’s interests encompass [[Magneto-optical drive|magneto‑optics]] and the statistical mechanics of soft matter, and her research profile has been highlighted in editorial roles and society memberships in journals and learned societies.<ref name=":0" /> She has supervised numerous graduate students guiding 13 to D.Phil. degrees at Oxford and 22 to Ph.D. degrees at Sheffield and continues to influence the field through research collaboration and mentorship.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards and honours ==

* 1992  Honorary DSc [[University of Salford]]<ref name=":1" />
* 2004 – Honorary Fellow, [[St Hugh's College, Oxford|St Hugh’s College, Oxford]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Gillian Gehring OBE |url=https://www.st-hughs.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-gillian-gehring/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=St Hugh's College |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* 2005 — OBE, [[2005 Birthday Honours]], for services to Physics and to Equal Opportunities.
* 2006 – [[Leverhulme Trust|Leverhulme Emeritus Fellowship]]<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2015-05-03 |title=The Lives and Times of Pioneering Women in Physics |url=https://helenthehare.org.uk/2015/05/03/the-lives-and-times-of-pioneering-women-in-physics-6/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=helen the hare |language=en}}</ref>
* 2009 – [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|Honorary Fellow, Institute of Physics]]<ref name=":2" />

* 2009 — [[Institute of Physics]] [[Nevill Mott Medal and Prize]]<ref name=":3" />
* 2010 – Honorary Member, [[European Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Gillian Gehring awarded an Honorary Doctor of Science at University of Hull |url=https://members.eps.org/blogpost/751263/160625/Professor-Gillian-Gehring-awarded-an-Honorary-Doctor-of-Science-at-University-of-Hull |website=EPS}}</ref>
* 2012 – Honorary D.Sc., [[University of Sheffield]]
* 2012 – Leverhulme Emeritus Fellowship<ref name=":4" />
* 2013 – Honorary D.Sc., [[University of Hull]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2019 – Featured cover scientist, [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] Magnetics Letters<ref name=":2" />

==Personal life==
She married on 5 October 1968 to Karl Adrian Gehring at Sherwood Congregational Church.<ref>''Nottingham Evening Post'' Tuesday 8 October 1968, page 6</ref> Karl Gehring grew up at 6 Newton St in [[Basford, Staffordshire|Basford]] in Stoke-on-Trent.<ref>''Staffordshire Sentinel'' Wednesday 18 July 1962, page 4</ref>
He went to [[Haberdashers' Adams|Adams' Grammar School]] in Newport, in [[Shropshire]].<ref>''Staffordshire Sentinel'' Monday 7 January 1957, page 4</ref> His father Ernst was from Switzerland, and had come to the UK in the war.<ref>''Staffordshire Sentinel'' Saturday 9 June 1973, page 5</ref> Ernest died on 3 November 1988, and had a wife Dorothy.<ref>''Staffordshire Sentinel'' Thursday 10 November 1988, page 4</ref>

She had two daughters in 1979 and 1981.{{citation needed|date=April 2021}}
